question.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to \infty }[g(t)+2f(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t) & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{1-{t}^{2}}\,i+(1+\frac{1}{t})\,j+{t}^{-2}\,k \\ g(t) & =2\,i+{e}^{-t}\,j+{(1+\frac{1}{t})}^{t}\,k\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \infty }f(t) & =({lim}_{t\to \infty }\frac{{t}^{2}}{1-{t}^{2}})\,i+({lim}_{t\to \infty }(1+\frac{1}{t}))\,j-({lim}_{t\to \infty }{t}^{-2})\,k, \\ {lim}_{t\to \infty }g(t) & =({lim}_{t\to \infty }2)\,i-({lim}_{t\to \infty }{e}^{-t})\,j+({lim}_{t\to \infty }{(1+\frac{1}{t})}^{t})\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's find the limits one-by-one.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {lim}_{t\to \infty }\frac{{t}^{2}}{1-{t}^{2}}={lim}_{t\to \infty }\frac{1}{\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}-1}=-1 \\  & {lim}_{t\to \infty }(1+\frac{1}{t})=1+{lim}_{t\to \infty }\frac{1}{t}=1 \\  & {lim}_{t\to \infty }{t}^{-2}={lim}_{t\to \infty }\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}=0 \\  & {lim}_{t\to \infty }2=2 \\  & {lim}_{t\to \infty }{e}^{-t}=0 \\  & {lim}_{t\to \infty }{(1+\frac{1}{t})}^{t}=e\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \infty }f(t) & =-1\,i+1\,j+0\,k \\  & =-i+j, \\ {lim}_{t\to \infty }g(t) & =2\,i+0\,j+e\,k \\  & =2\,i+e\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to \infty }[g(t)+2f(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to \infty }g(t)+2{lim}_{t\to \infty }f(t) \\  & =(2\,i+e\,k)+2(-i+j) \\  & =2j+e\,k\end{aligned}
$$
